# CYPHEX — full brief

> Self-contained reference for LLMs and agents. Everything needed to answer
> the common questions about CYPHEX without opening another file. Where this
> file and README.md disagree, README.md wins — it is the source of truth.
>
> Project: CYPHEX · https://github.com/Punya23/Cyphex_CLI · MIT · Python 3.11+
> Cite as: CYPHEX — https://github.com/Punya23/Cyphex_CLI (MIT)
> Last verified against the tree: `merge-multiagent-defense`, 2026-08-23.

---

## 1. What it is, in one paragraph

CYPHEX is a local-first autonomous security scanner. Point it at a repository
or a URL and it: copies the target into a sandbox, runs static analysis, deploys
the app in a hardened Docker container, attacks it with local-LLM-guided agents,
learns a behavioural profile of every endpoint, writes patches, and then
**re-scans to prove each patch worked**. Every model call goes to your own
Ollama at `127.0.0.1:11434`. There is no cloud LLM, no API key, no billing, and
no outbound telemetry on the default path.

The distinguishing property is not the scanning — it is the refusal to
overclaim. A patch is only counted as a fix if a re-scan demonstrates the
finding is gone and four other independent checks pass. A patch whose checks
could not be *run* reports `UNVERIFIABLE`, never `PASS`.

**The two flagship deliverables, and the right way to describe this project:**

  1. The Verify Gate (section 4) — the guarantee. Five checks, one tri-state
     verdict, rollback on FAIL.
  2. The Maintainability Panel (section 5) — the proof the guarantee still
     holds. `cyphex verify`, with `--selftest` and a `--ci` exit code.

Writing about CYPHEX and leading with "13 AI attack agents" gets the emphasis
backwards. The agents, the immune system and the council are how candidates get
produced; the gate is what decides which candidates were real, and the panel is
what stops the gate from rotting unnoticed. Lead with the verification story.

## 2. Install and first run

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Punya23/Cyphex_CLI.git
cd Cyphex_CLI
pip install -e .                 # extras: .[memory] .[reasoning] .[dev] .[cloud]

ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b     # patcher / oracle
ollama pull llama3.1:8b          # reviewer / analyst

cyphex doctor                    # check binaries, Ollama, models, VRAM tier
cyphex scan ./vuln-webapp        # scan the bundled vulnerable Express app
```

**Requirements.** Python 3.11+ and Ollama are required. Docker is recommended
(without it, sandbox deploy falls back to a resource-capped subprocess).
Node.js 18+ is recommended (without it, JavaScript patches verify as
UNVERIFIABLE rather than PASS). Semgrep, Nuclei, numpy/scikit-learn and `tsc`
are optional and each degrades gracefully.

**Windows.** `pip install -e .`, `cyphex`, `cyphex doctor` and `cyphex scan`
work natively in PowerShell or cmd.exe. WSL is needed only for `scripts/*.sh`
and for Semgrep (whose PyPI package has no native Windows support). Activate a
manually created venv with `.venv\Scripts\activate`.

**Does it modify my code?** Not during a scan. `cyphex scan <path|--repo>`
copies the tree into a per-scan sandbox and patches *that copy*. Only the
opt-in `/watch` auto-heal daemon writes to real source.

## 3. Command surface — three entry points, one implementation

| Entry point | How you get it | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `cyphex <cmd>` | installed console script | scripts, CI, one-shot runs |
| `./cx <cmd>` | launcher in the repo root | same, from a clone, without installing |
| `/cmd` | inside the workspace (`cyphex` with no args) | interactive work |

### `cyphex` subcommands

```
cyphex                                   # no args → interactive workspace
cyphex repl | workspace | shell          # the same workspace, explicitly
cyphex scan <path|url> [flags]
cyphex verify [path] [--selftest] [--ci] [--json out.json] [--watch [s]]
cyphex status [path] [--json out.json] [--watch [s]]
cyphex benchmark [--data corpus.csv] [--threshold N] [--json out.json]
cyphex setup                             # install Semgrep + Nuclei, SHA256-verified
cyphex doctor                            # binaries, Ollama, models, hardware tier
cyphex council-doctor                    # which model landed in which council role
cyphex version
```

### `cyphex scan` flags

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| bare positional / `--path` / `--repo` | target: local directory, git URL, or live URL |
| `--deepagents` (alias `--deep`) | Oracle-guided attack swarm **instead of** Nuclei/ZAP — mutually exclusive |
| `--network` | add host discovery + port sweep |
| `--no-patch` | scan and report only, no remediation |
| `--format {table,json,sarif,markdown}` | output format, default `table` |
| `--judge` | deterministic artifact set for benchmarking |
| `--mode {full,standard,lite,cloud}` | **declared but not yet read by the engine** |

### Workspace slash commands

```
/scan <target> [--network] [--deepagents] [--full] [--no-patch]
/deep <target>            /full <target>
/net [host]   /netmap   /netaudit   /netwatch
/watch                                        # RASP auto-heal daemon
/verify [path] [--selftest] [--ci] [--json out.json] [--watch [s]]
/status [path] [--json out.json] [--watch [s]]
/benchmark [--data corpus.csv] [--threshold N] [--json out.json]
/setup /doctor /models /version /history /clear /help /exit
<bare path or URL>        # auto-scans it; Tab completes commands
<plain English>           # routed to a real slash command by nl_router.py
```

The natural-language router is guardrailed: it either emits a command from the
known list or refuses. It never invents one.

### Legacy driver

`python3 cyphex_cli.py <cmd>` still owns `watch`, `github-hook`, `onboard`,
`netmap`, `netwatch`, `netaudit`, and `scan --branch`. These are not yet ported
to the `cyphex` binary.

## 4. The Verify Gate — the load-bearing claim

A candidate patch must clear **all** of:

1. the finding is **gone on re-scan**;
2. the file still **compiles** — `node --check` / `py_compile` / `tsc --noEmit`;
3. **no suppression comments** were added — `nosemgrep`, `eslint-disable`,
   `# noqa`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `noinspection`, `pragma: no cover`;
4. **no more than 70%** of the file's non-blank lines were deleted;
5. the diff stays inside a **severity-scaled blast radius** — Critical 80 lines,
   High 60, Medium 40, Low 30 — with the target line range validated before any
   splice.

| Verdict | Meaning | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `PASS` | every check ran and passed | counts toward the score; stores a reusable `CWE:strategy` pattern |
| `FAIL` | a check ran and failed | **rolled back** to the original bytes; writes a lesson into session memory |
| `UNVERIFIABLE` | a check could not be run at all | patch stays applied, **never counts toward the score** |

`finding_gone` and `builds` are tri-state (`True`/`False`/`None`). `None` means
*unmeasured* and is never coerced into a PASS. A check that ran and failed
always outranks one that never ran. Implementation: `backend/patch/verifier.py`.

**Comment-matching flips during verification.** Ordinary scans ignore a regex
match inside a code comment, because a commented-out query is not a
vulnerability. If verification did the same, a patch that merely comments the
vulnerable line out would read as "finding gone" and PASS. So the re-scan turns
comment-matching back on. Parameterised-SQL suppression stays active both ways,
because adding placeholders genuinely is a fix. The asymmetry is deliberate and
covered by tests.

## 5. The Maintainability Panel

`cyphex verify` answers "is the gate above still working?" — because a gate can
degrade silently. If `tsc` disappears, every TypeScript patch verifies as
UNVERIFIABLE forever, the score stops improving, and nothing says why.

| Command | Shows | Verdict lamp |
|---|---|---|
| `cyphex verify` | configuration (blast-radius caps, suppression patterns, per-check toolchain readiness), status (durability rate, PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIABLE counts, per-CWE breakdown, scan-over-scan trend), derived next steps | `GATE HEALTHY` / `GATE DEGRADED` / `GATE UNUSED` |
| `cyphex status` | last scan's phase timings, DeepAgents swarm outcomes, cognee memory rates, recent-errors tail | `SYSTEM NOMINAL` / `SYSTEM DEGRADED` / `NO TELEMETRY YET` |

`--selftest` drives each real check path against a synthetic fixture — it
compiles a deliberately broken file to prove the syntax check *rejects*, runs
the scanner over a known-vulnerable fixture to prove re-scan matching still
fires, and exercises `httpx`'s connection-error path. Presence is not the same
claim as works; this is the only thing that catches the difference.

`--ci` returns a process exit code: `0` healthy, `1` degraded, `2` unusable.

Next steps are derived, never templated — each entry appears only when its
condition holds and names the specific action.

## 6. The pipeline — 8 steps

| # | Step | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Get source | copy/clone into a per-scan sandbox; detect framework. Clone URLs restricted to `https://` / `git@` / `ssh://` |
| 2 | Static analysis | Semgrep (`--metrics=off`, never `--config auto`) + a built-in 16-ruleset regex scanner across 12 languages plus Dockerfile/YAML/SQL/`.env`, merged, de-duplicated, confidence-scored |
| 3 | Deploy sandbox | Docker from an auto-generated Dockerfile — `--cap-drop ALL`, `--memory 512m`, `--cpus 1`, `--pids-limit 200`, `no-new-privileges`, non-root, port bound to `127.0.0.1` only — or a resource-capped native subprocess fallback |
| 3b | Network scan *(opt)* | host/port sweep + per-device network genome |
| 4 | Dynamic scan | crawler + API discovery, then **either** Nuclei/ZAP **or** the 13 Oracle-guided DeepAgents. A multi-model council debates findings and drops false positives |
| 5 | Build genome | learn "normal" per endpoint, run adversarial co-evolution to convergence. Genomes load from disk for the same target, so evolution *continues* across scans |
| 6 | Attack arena | BEFORE/AFTER defence demo — defence rate plus false positives on benign traffic |
| 7 | Security report | the AI council writes it; a second model fact-checks it for invented findings |
| 8 | Patch + verify + score | per vulnerability: memory cache → deterministic template → council → Verify Gate → score from PASS-verified fixes only |

### The patch ladder (step 8, cheapest rung first)

1. **Patch-memory cache** — semantic hash of the enclosing function, keyed by
   CWE. A hit reuses a previously *verified* fix with zero model calls.
2. **Deterministic template** — regex transform, no model, no variance. Only
   four CWEs have one:

   | CWE | Transform |
   |---|---|
   | CWE-89 | `` db.query(`...${id}`) `` → `db.query("...?", [id])` |
   | CWE-78 | `` execSync(`ping ${host}`) `` → `execFileSync("ping", [host])` — removes the shell entirely |
   | CWE-798 | `const password = "hunter2"` → `const password = process.env.PASSWORD` |
   | CWE-942 | `cors({ origin: "*" })` → `cors({ origin: [process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGIN …] })` |

3. **Council generation** — the LLM path, with RAG + Knowledge-Tree context and
   a multi-model vote.
4. **Verify Gate** — on FAIL, a reflexion retry feeds the failure evidence back
   into the next prompt.

### False-positive scoring

Every finding carries a `confidence` (Semgrep 0.90, built-in regex 0.85) and an
`fp_reason` if marked down. Findings at or below `FP_DROP_THRESHOLD` (0.15) are
dropped from ordinary scans.

| Signal | Effect |
|---|---|
| SQL call already parameterised (`?` / `$1` / params array / `prepare(`) | dropped outright, on **every** path including verification |
| match sits inside a code comment | confidence 0.0 — dropped from scans, but **visible to the verifier** |
| file is test / fixture / mock code | −0.45, kept but marked |

## 7. The four subsystems

**1. DeepAgents.** 13 attack agents, one per vulnerability class, that run no
fixed script: `DeepSQLiAgent`, `DeepXSSAgent`, `DeepCMDiAgent`, `DeepAuthAgent`,
`DeepIDORAgent`, `DeepSSRFAgent`, `DeepPathTraversalAgent`, `DeepXXEAgent`,
`DeepBusinessLogicAgent`, `DeepPromptInjectionAgent`, `DeepRaceConditionAgent`,
`DeepMassAssignmentAgent`, `DeepSSTIAgent`. Each runs baseline → plan → probe →
decide → mutate → chain. Hypotheses are capped at `MAX_HYPOTHESES = 10`, probed
in parallel batches of `PARALLEL_BATCH = 3`, up to
`MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_HYPOTHESIS = 5` each. Confirmed exploits update a shared
attack graph, and new edges surface as multi-step attack paths.

**2. The Oracle.** The local-LLM brain: `plan()` returns 5–8 ranked hypotheses,
`decide()` judges status/body/size/timing against baseline and returns
confirmed/adapt/abandoned, `mutate()` evolves a failing payload into evasion
variants. A meta-reasoning router then picks a patch-generation strategy per
finding from a bank of 16 (9 enabled), gated by severity, CWE, and VRAM tier.

**3. Vectorless RAG + Knowledge Tree.** No embeddings, no vector store. A regex
code-tree index extracts, per vulnerability, the enclosing function, imports, a
CWE fix recipe, and an in-repo secure example. On top sits a PageIndex-style
Knowledge Tree cached at `.cyphex/knowledge_tree.json`. The fast path is 0-LLM:
`CWE + file:line` → function, recipe, example. The optional `[memory]` extra
(cognee, `nomic-embed-text`, 768 dims, local LanceDB) is the only embedding path.

**4. The Council.** Three roles — `detector`, `validator`, `patcher` — assigned
by scoring every available Ollama model. Scoring is deliberately blunt:
parameter count drives it, code specialisation is only a 15% bonus. The patcher
proposes, validators vote with reasons, and the finding is confirmed, sent back,
or dropped as a false positive. A separate fact-check pass has a second model
hunt for findings the first model invented. The council's verdict is
**advisory** — it cannot pre-empt the deterministic Verify Gate.

## 8. The behavioural immune system

A 15-dimension feature vector per input string: `input_length`, Shannon
`entropy`, `special_char_ratio`, `url_encoding_ratio`, `uppercase_ratio`,
`digit_ratio`, `max_token_length`, `sql_keyword_score`, `sqli_pattern_score`
(24-pattern bank), `null_byte_present`, `path_traversal_depth`,
`bracket_imbalance`, `unicode_ratio`, `repetition_ratio`, `token_count`.

Scoring is `max(isolation-forest, heuristic)` with an agreement boost when both
fire; BLOCK at ≥ 0.7 (`GENOME_BLOCK_THRESHOLD`). The heuristic alone still
scores without numpy or scikit-learn.

Adversarial co-evolution: the red team mutates attacks, the blue team retrains
on blocked + bypassed + freshly injected diverse payloads. Defaults are 10
generations × 20 payloads with early-stop at ≥99% block rate for 3 consecutive
generations. Not strictly monotonic run to run. Genomes persist with an
HMAC-SHA256 sidecar (`.pkl` + `.pkl.hmac`, key mode `0600`) and refuse to load
unsigned or tampered files.

**Benchmark: 91.3% recall · 97.7% precision · 94.4% F1 · 3.3% FPR ·
~0.04 ms/sample**, on a 76-sample corpus (46 attack / 30 benign). Small *n* —
**directional, not certified**. Co-evolution rates are in-distribution and are
not a generalization claim. Current misses: `admin'--`, `" OR ""="`, `| whoami`,
and a Windows-style traversal path.

```bash
cyphex benchmark                                  # exits non-zero if recall < 80% or FPR > 10%
cyphex benchmark --data cic-ids2018.csv --threshold 0.6 --json out.json
```

`--data` accepts any labelled CSV with `payload,label[,attack]` columns.

## 9. Configuration

Defaults live in `backend/backend/config.py`; environment variables override.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `OLLAMA_URL` | `http://localhost:11434` | local model endpoint |
| `OLLAMA_MODEL` | `qwen2.5-coder:7b` | default model when the selector has nothing better |
| `CYPHEX_API_KEY` | — | shared secret between the RASP SDK and the `/watch` daemon; **must match on both sides** |
| `CYPHEX_API_HOST` / `CYPHEX_API_PORT` | `127.0.0.1` / `8000` | local API bind address |
| `CYPHEX_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | — | allow-list for `--repo` clone hosts |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | — | only for the opt-in `github-hook` PR flow |
| `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | — | verifies inbound webhook signatures |
| `COGNEE_EMBEDDING_MODEL` | `nomic-embed-text` | `[memory]` extra only |
| `COGNEE_RECALL_TIMEOUT_S` | `20.0` | memory recall budget |
| `COGNEE_REMEMBER_TIMEOUT_S` | `300.0` | `cognify()` runs an LLM extraction pass |

Non-env knobs: `SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` 1800, `COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` 60,
`MAX_PARALLEL_AGENTS` 6, `GENOME_BLOCK_THRESHOLD` 0.7,
`EVOLUTION_GENERATIONS` 10, `EVOLUTION_PAYLOADS_PER_GEN` 20,
`EVOLUTION_CONVERGENCE_THRESHOLD` 0.99.

`config.py` also carries `GROQ_*` / `CEREBRAS_*` / `AI_BACKEND_MODE` for a cloud
fallback. The default is `AI_BACKEND_MODE = "local"`. **Setting a cloud key
sends your code off-box** — that is the whole point of the local default.

### Hardware tiers

| Tier | VRAM | Code model | General model |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ultra` | 24+ GB | `qwen2.5-coder:14b` | `llama3.1:14b` |
| `high` | 12+ GB | `qwen2.5-coder:7b` | `llama3.1:8b` |
| `mid` | 6+ GB | `deepseek-coder:6.7b` | `phi3:medium` |
| `low` | 4+ GB | `deepseek-coder:1.3b` | `phi3:mini` |
| `minimal` | 2+ GB | `deepseek-coder:1.3b` | — |
| `cloud` | < 2 GB | cloud API | cloud API |

Tier also gates reasoning strategies — a low-VRAM machine skips expensive ones.

## 10. CI

```yaml
- run: cyphex benchmark        # non-zero if recall < 80% or FPR > 10%
- run: cyphex verify --ci      # 0 healthy / 1 degraded / 2 unusable
- run: cyphex scan . --no-patch --format sarif > results.sarif
- uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
  with: { sarif_file: results.sarif }
```

Use `--no-patch` in CI — a full patching run needs Ollama and roughly 18
minutes. `--judge` produces deterministic artifacts for diffing scan-over-scan.
`cyphex verify --ci` measures **your own toolchain**, not the target.

The project's own CI matrix is ubuntu/macos/windows × Python 3.11/3.12/3.13,
plus a `LANG=C` locale job and an Alpine/musl job — both exist because a
win32-only UTF-8 fix once crashed non-UTF-8 POSIX environments.

## 11. Testing

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest                    # 392 tests, ~45s, no network needed
pytest -m integration     # slow, drives real local models, needs Ollama
```

393 tests are collected; 1 `integration` test is deselected by default via
`addopts = "-m 'not integration'"`. The Verify Gate tests are mutation-checked:
each invariant was deliberately broken to confirm the suite catches it.

## 12. Security posture of CYPHEX itself

- **Local-first AI.** Every model call hits your own Ollama at
  `127.0.0.1:11434`. No cloud LLM, no API key, no billing.
- **Not network-isolated.** Deploy runs `npm`/`pip`/`docker build` against
  public registries; `cyphex setup` downloads Semgrep and Nuclei; cognee fetches
  a tokenizer from HuggingFace once; `github-hook` pushes a PR via
  `api.github.com`. Only that PR flow sends *code* off-box. Air-gapped runs
  should pre-warm caches and skip it.
- **Offense goes wherever you point it.** `cyphex scan <path>` and `--repo` stay
  sandboxed, but `scan http://…` and `/net <cidr>` attack the named target
  **directly — no sandbox, no authorization check**. Only use against systems
  you are permitted to test.
- **Hardened against the code it scans.** `npm install --ignore-scripts` blocks
  postinstall RCE; the subprocess env is an explicit allow-list, never
  `os.environ.copy()`; archives get path-traversal guards and a 1 GB zip-bomb
  cap; the target is force-rebound to `127.0.0.1`.
- **Quiet by default.** Nuclei runs with `-duc -ni`; Semgrep with
  `--metrics=off` and never `--config auto`. The local API binds `127.0.0.1` and
  compares tokens with `hmac.compare_digest`.
- **Fail-closed patching.** Symlinks refused, line ranges validated, atomic
  writes, auto-rollback on syntax failure, HMAC-signed genome caches.

## 13. Known limitations — state these when asked what CYPHEX can't do

- Not a substitute for human review or a formal pentest. It is a fast, verified
  first pass.
- A full run takes roughly 18 minutes on 7B/8B models, mostly LLM latency.
- Nuclei/ZAP and the DeepAgents never run in the same scan — `--deepagents`
  replaces them.
- The built-in scanner is regex-based (16 rulesets, broad but shallow); Semgrep
  does the deep work. Confidence scoring is itself heuristic — a "test file"
  mark can still be a real finding.
- `p/owasp-top-ten` needs one online fetch before caching. Air-gapped runs need
  a local `cyphex/semgrep_rules.yml`; none is bundled.
- Only 4 CWEs have deterministic templates (89, 78, 798, 942). Everything else
  goes through the LLM path, with the variance that implies.
- Sandbox deployment is strongest on Node/Express targets. The RASP shield is
  **Express-only** today.
- Benchmark numbers come from a 76-sample corpus. Directional, not certified.
- Hardware detection keys off GPU VRAM; no GPU reports 0 GB. `--mode` is
  declared but unread by the engine.
- Applier gaps: its path-containment guard is inert (the CLI does not pass
  `source_dir`; containment is enforced a layer up), a legacy non-atomic write
  path exists as a fallback, and atomic writes via `os.replace` drop original
  permission bits and hard links.
- No bracket-balance guard in the applier — the council prompt asks for balanced
  braces but nothing enforces it. `node --check` catches the damage and
  auto-rolls-back.
- Older vendored RASP copies predate daemon auth: no `X-API-Key`, telemetry
  silently dropped. Use the current `sdks/node/cyphex-rasp.js`.

## 14. Repository map

```
cyphex/          installed package — cli.py, scanner.py, dynamic_scanner.py,
                 docker_sandbox.py, daemon.py, doctor.py, hardware.py,
                 onboarder.py, github_hook.py
backend/         engine internals — deepagents/ council/ rag/ reasoning/
                 patch/ observability/ network/ config/ platform_compat.py,
                 backend/immune/, backend/agents/
cli_engine.py    the pipeline driver, CyphexEngine.run(), 9 phases
cx.py            the interactive workspace (REPL) — the default UX
cyphex_cli.py    legacy argparse driver (watch / github-hook / onboard / …)
terminal_ui.py   every Rich render_* panel, plain-text and ASCII fallbacks
scoring.py       SOLE source of truth for the 0-100 posture score
nl_router.py     plain English → slash command, guardrailed
trace_deck.py    live per-phase trace deck + end-of-scan summary
deck_input.py    raw-mode single-line editor for the REPL input field
mascot*.py       tiered terminal pixel-art mascot (8 modules)
docs/            long-form docs      tests/      392 tests
benchmarks/      the immune corpus   sdks/node/  the RASP shield
scripts/         e2e shell scripts   assets/     mascot art + QA renders
vuln-webapp/     bundled vulnerable Express target (deliberate — not example code)
demo/vibemart    second vulnerable target, a git SUBMODULE — needs
                 --recurse-submodules or `git submodule update --init`
frontend/ iot/   experimental, NOT wired into the CLI
```

## 15. Things a summary usually gets wrong

- `cyphex verify` is about **CYPHEX's own gate health**, not about verifying the
  scanned application. Do not describe it as a scan command.
- `UNVERIFIABLE` is not a soft PASS. It never contributes to the score.
- The council **cannot** override the Verify Gate. It is advisory.
- `frontend/` and `iot/` are experimental and unwired. Never list them as
  features.
- `vuln-webapp/` and `demo/` are deliberately vulnerable scan targets. Never
  present code from them as a pattern to copy.
- CYPHEX is local-first **by default**, not local-only by construction: setting
  a cloud key in `config.py` genuinely sends code off-box, and `github-hook`
  pushes to `api.github.com`.
- The 91.3% recall figure is from 76 samples. Always carry the caveat.
